### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **10** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/account-invitation-marker.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-schema-config.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os migrate account-issuer (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/account-issuer.ts))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via os migrate account-issuer (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/account-issuer.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **10** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/account-invitation-marker.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-schema-config.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **153** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9239b2b7624186eca71a88372dec3f612ce9fa17` — the merge of head `ea86e485634d247bbd29f39c0984ba11a0abfa66` into base `f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9239b2b7624186eca71a88372dec3f612ce9fa17 && git checkout 9239b2b7624186eca71a88372dec3f612ce9fa17
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55 ea86e485634d247bbd29f39c0984ba11a0abfa66 && git checkout -B drift-repro f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55 && git merge --no-ff ea86e485634d247bbd29f39c0984ba11a0abfa66

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ea86e485634d247bbd29f39c0984ba11a0abfa66`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/identity/organization.zod.ts + pnpm-workspace.yaml, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, .changeset/25096-better-auth-1-7-12.md, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/session-read-failure-answer.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/verification-reservation-single-use.test.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/sqlite-driver-fallback-file-open-failure.test.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/sqlite-driver-fallback.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/account-issuer.ts

Inputs: card #25096 (body and all 13 comments), PR #25109 (body, 24-file list, net diff against the merge base `ae58b26f9c`), and the check-runs on this head. Read-only throughout: `git show` / `git diff` on the fetched branch, the REST API, and a line-based read of the two `pnpm-lock.yaml` blobs; nothing was built, tested or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The 16 pins — right.** `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: all 11 family overrides (`better-auth`, `@better-auth/core`, `scim`, `oauth-provider`, `sso`, `drizzle-adapter`, `kysely-adapter`, `memory-adapter`, `mongo-adapter`, `prisma-adapter`, `telemetry`) move `1.7.3` to `1.7.12`, exact; every selector keeps its below-2.0.0 major bound and the header's selector rule is untouched (one header sentence loses a literal `1.7.2`, prose only). `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json`: the five declared ranges move to exact `1.7.12`, no caret. No other manifest in the workspace names a better-auth package. The family's comment note states the delta measured in item 2 and matches it.
2. **Lockfile delta — right, and confined as the PR claims.** Measured on the `packages:` keys of the two blobs: 40 removed, 13 added. Added = the 11 family packages at 1.7.12, `better-call@1.4.4`, `@better-fetch/fetch@1.3.2`, nothing else. Removed = the 11 at 1.7.3, `better-call@1.4.0`, `@better-fetch/fetch@1.3.1`, `@better-auth/utils@0.4.2` (0.5.0 stays as the only copy; every 1.7.12 family package peers `^0.4.2 || ^0.5.0`), `better-sqlite3@12.11.1` and the 20 packages only its native build pulled (`bindings`, `prebuild-install`, `node-abi`, `tar-fs`, `rc`, `ini`, `pump`, `simple-get` and the rest), `@cloudflare/workers-types` and `@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions` (their only dependent on main was `@better-auth/core@1.7.3`), and two dedups, `@noble/ciphers@2.3.0` (2.4.0 stays, the range `service-settings` declares) and `tldts` / `tldts-core@7.4.9` (7.4.16 stays). Importers: plugin-auth's five specifiers, plus the `apps/account` / `apps/setup` vitest rows exchanging the two existing `vite@8.3.4` peer variants (esbuild 0.28.1 / 0.28.2) — no version enters or leaves. Zero dangling edges at head: every snapshot and importer dependency resolves to a snapshot key. **Nothing removed is still needed**: no manifest, tsconfig or source file at head names any of the 22 removed package names (import, require and `types` forms grepped); `bindings` was the one hidden-hoist consumer and is the round-3 fix. `Validate Package Dependencies`, `Build Core` and every Lint and Type Check lane installed this lockfile frozen and concluded `success`.
3. **Route ledger — right.** One row, `POST /api/v1/auth/oauth2/client/rotate-keys`, with its measured answer (`403 access_denied`; `allowClientKeyRotation` unset) in the comment. The vendor publishes the route through plugin-auth's catch-all, the ledger's mounted-surface equality is exactly the pin a lift should redden, and the ledger stays truthful (rule 4, Route & surface ownership).
4. **Two new pins — right.** Both boot the real stack (ObjectQL over driver-sql, the manifest's objects, a real AuthManager), import workspace packages only (no escaping path reads), keep controls beside the failure legs, and pin the vendor property plugin-auth now depends on: a store failure answers 500 `FAILED_TO_GET_SESSION` and keeps the cookie (not the 1.7.3 `401`), and the ObjectQL adapter keeps the forced reservation id so a replay is refused. The PR body records one ablation leg per pin, each going red on the committed code.
5. **`packages/spec` hunk — prose only.** Three lines inside the `updatedAt` property's TSDoc, appending the 1.7.12 re-measurement after the 1.7.3 reading, as ruled. The `.describe()` string, the Zod shape and every key are unchanged; the TSDoc sentence appears in no generated artifact on main (grepped), so no `check:docs` or authorable-surface artifact moves and none is in the diff. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true for spec.
6. **`packages/cli` description — right.** The operator-facing sentence loses the version and carries no tracker number; no test pins it.
7. **`service-datasource` — right.** `realNotBuiltFailure()` now requires the absent `build/Release/better_sqlite3.node` under the test's scratch directory, through a require seeded at the installed `better-sqlite3` resolved from `@objectstack/driver-sql` (a declared dependency): Node answers `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, the code the 13.x loader meets with no prebuild and no build, and the case asserts that code instead of `toBeUndefined()`. No phantom dependency remains; the unused `dirname` import is dropped. The `sqlite-driver-fallback.ts` change is comment-only — every changed line is a docblock line and no code moves — and that docblock ships in `dist/index.d.ts`, which is why the package rides the changeset.
8. **Attestations — right.** The 13 remaining plugin-auth files change comments only: 19 lines restamped with the re-measurement, 12 kept as facts about the 1.7.3 release, and `internal-field-readback.ts` flags its `identifier` census as wrong in place instead of restamping it (the `READBACK_FIELDS` table is unchanged; the finding is reported for filing). The lint lane carrying `check-vendor-version-stamps` concluded `success`.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/25096-better-auth-1-7-12.md`**: four entries, all `patch` (`plugin-auth`, `spec`, `cli`, `service-datasource`; none is private). Line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` sit in the changeset body and in the PR body. Under AGENTS.md item 3 as it reads on `main` (ruling A on #25105, landed by PR #25114), `none` takes `patch` on every entry and a non-protocol breaking change keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition at `patch` — which is what the file does: the banner is kept and its sentence states `patch` under ruling A; exactly one disposition marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category in the gate's `CATEGORIES`; the head's `Check Changeset` run passed its ADR-0087 step and annotated that exemption. The level is right, and ruling `6317990662` is carried out to the letter: the round-4 commit touches three lines of the changeset and nothing else.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — the right arm.** The lift narrows: new refusals (`PASSWORD_TOO_LONG`, OIDC `issuer_mismatch`, an ID token without `exp` / `iat`), a status move (PKCE 401 to 400), in-flight flows invalidated. The adversarial reading, `yes (narrowing)` ("widens one surface and narrows another"), was taken on the two candidates. The DPoP `htu` re-binding swaps one accept set for another (the request URL for the configured public URL plus path); the two coincide wherever the request host equals the base URL and are equal-sized where they differ — a replacement, not a superset — so ruling `6315255713` Q2 (A) stands. The newly mounted `rotate-keys` path grows the public face by one route that refuses every call unconditionally (the option that would open it is unset), so it admits nothing and `no` on 「放宽接受集」 holds; the ledger row is the declaration of the face change. Under ruling A the arm moves the level neither way.
- **FROM / TO and operator notes against the measurements.** Each FROM / TO maps to a measured reading in the PR body: identifier prefixes (probe), `get-session` 500 (pin and ablation), PKCE 400 (probe), `PASSWORD_TOO_LONG` with the lockout count (probe), both DPoP halves (probe), stale-cookie clearing (probe), `rotate-keys` 403 (suite), the Unchanged list (probes and suites). One FROM / TO rests on the vendor rather than on this stack: the OIDC `issuer_mismatch` refusal and the `exp` / `iat` requirement are not in the measurement table. both are confirmed in the published 1.7.12 dists read for this review: `issuer_mismatch` in `@better-auth/sso` (a `400` naming the discovered and configured issuers), and the `exp` / `iat` requirement in `@better-auth/core`'s `oauth2/verify-id-token.mjs` (`ID_TOKEN_REQUIRED_CLAIMS` is `iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `exp`, `iat`, passed to jose as `requiredClaims`), so the sentence is true of 1.7.12 even though neither leg was driven on this stack. The operator notes carry both items the card's acceptance 5 prescribes (restart in-flight Magic Link / OAuth / SAML flows; set an OIDC issuer to the exact discovery value), plus client notes for PKCE and `get-session`. The dependency sentence (`better-call` 1.4.4, `@better-auth/utils` 0.5.0, `@better-fetch/fetch` 1.3.2) matches the lockfile. Nothing claims more than is true, and the card's own `patch` ask is met after the ruling-A regrade.
- The one shared body means the `spec`, `cli` and `service-datasource` CHANGELOGs will carry the `fix(plugin-auth)!:` entry with its BREAKING banner; the body says in its own words that those three are text-only and not breaking. Acceptable under the seat's "ride as `patch`" ruling; a separate non-breaking changeset would have been cleaner, not required.

The stamp gate does not read these shapes (it is green), `init.test.ts` pins the entries' presence, and `allowedVersions` only suppresses a report, so the scaffold resolves identically — a stale ledger, not a defect in this PR. A card for the cli lane, with the test pins to flip alongside.
